methods.name: Odd-N BRC admissible multiplier scan / strong square-gap cascade
capabilities: safe deletion of all m congruent 2 mod 4 for odd-N difference-of-squares search
exact m->m+2 retained-root/remainder transport with at most three BRC basin corrections
zero-false-negative two-table squarehood prefilter using moduli 20160 and 46189
experimental static multiplier ranking from admissible nontrivial divisor-ratio count
methods.core_law: For odd N, m==2 mod 4 cannot satisfy x^2-y^2=mN. The admissible monotone path therefore has 75 states through m<=100. One-step transitions reuse t0.brc_multiplier_transition; two-step skips use a dyadic sqrt((m+2)/m) predictor and at most three odd-width corrections. A square gap must pass both mod-20160 and mod-46189 tables, whose uniform joint pass fraction is 108/46189.
methods.hard_boundary: Parity pruning, quadratic-residue filtering, Lawrence/Lehman/Hart multiplier-Fermat search, and rational factor-ratio selection are classical prior art. The nu(m)^4/m priority is experimental only and is not a theorem, default proof path, RSA shortcut, or asymptotic improvement. Finite timings and finite hit-rate samples do not imply factorization complexity progress. The BRC-specific proved addition is retained-state m->m+2 transport and its composition with the existing multiplier transition tool.

methods.name: BRC mod-8 sparse multiplier transition
capabilities: exact root/remainder transport only on the odd-N mod-8 scan representatives
deterministic compilation of lower two-step dyadic predictors from adjacent canonical one-step constants
root-free remainder update for multiplier steps one and two
proved two-correction bound for step one and four-correction bound for compiled step two
exact 62-state m<=100 root stream instead of 100 consecutive states
methods.core_law: The scan-complete multiplier residues {0,1,3,5,7} mod 8 have adjacent gaps only 1 or 2. If A_m/2^B and A_(m+1)/2^B are lower dyadic bounds for the consecutive square-root scale factors, floor(A_m A_(m+1)/2^B)/2^B is a lower bound for sqrt((m+2)/m). With J_m<2^(B-1), this compiled predictor places the exact two-step root at most four square-basin crossings above the candidate. Therefore statically removed multipliers need not have BRC root states materialized.
methods.hard_boundary: The checked-in production sequence reuses the current canonical transition table and is therefore bounded at max_multiplier<=100. Long-stream rows in the research note used separately generated consecutive constants and demonstrate the construction, not a larger production table. This is an exact constant-factor transport improvement only; it does not reduce the Hart/Lehman N^(1/3) search horizon or imply asymptotic factorization speedup.

methods.name: BRC multiplier 2-adic strip normalization
capabilities: safe deletion of m==2 mod4 impossible strips
safe reduction of m==4 mod8 square-scaled strips to m/4
methods.core_law: For odd N: m==2 mod4 is impossible for x^2-y^2=mN; m==4 mod8 forces x,y even and every hit divides to (m/4)N with parent vertical offset floor(t/2); for m odd or 8|m explicit representations show that no universal factor-two reduction is forced. Through m<=100 this yields 25 impossible, 13 redundant-by-four, and 62 universally 2-adically primitive strips.
methods.hard_boundary: This is elementary classical parity/congruence content expressed in BRC coordinates. Lehman's original inner loop already uses parity/mod-4 restrictions and different strides. The result does not improve the classical Lehman exponent or claim new factoring mathematics; it canonicalizes the arbitrary-multiplier BRC search and prevents duplicate strips. No Foundation promotion is made.

methods.name: BRC multi-strip smooth-relation lattice / GF(2) carrier facade
capabilities: exact cross-multiplier relation extraction x^2-D=mN with shared x^2=D mod N semantics
exact B-smooth factorization carrier with full exponent and parity projections
incremental GF(2) dependency detection retaining relation provenance
exact square-congruence reconstruction and gcd witness surface
round-robin shallow relation sampling across all admissible multiplier strips
methods.core_law: Every smooth BRC lattice point x_i^2-D_i=m_i N gives x_i^2 congruent D_i mod N, so relations from different multiplier strips combine in one factor-base algebra without any condition on the product of multiplier labels. The exponent parity projection is sufficient for GF(2) dependency detection, but full exponents and x provenance must be retained to reconstruct the square congruence. Multiplier provenance may be forgotten only after relation extraction when future operations are restricted to dependency/congruence construction.
methods.hard_boundary: Dixon, QS, MPQS, SIQS, B-smooth factor-base collection, GF(2) linear algebra and congruence-of-squares factoring are classical prior art. The reference implementation uses trial division and incremental bitset elimination and is not a production sieve. Finite relation-yield/factoring-budget improvements are not asymptotic complexity results or novelty claims. The minimum-gap heap optimizes only next-gap ordering, not proved smoothness probability. No Foundation promotion is made.

unique mod-m power-free skeleton and rational thickness
unique rooted spanning-tree rational gauge normal form
methods.core_law: Q_{>0}^x is free abelian on primes; rational vertex gauge acts by primewise integer coboundaries. Every q>0 has unique q=s_m*t^m, and a rooted spanning tree uniquely fixes tree weights to one so non-tree weights are complete fundamental rational holonomies.
methods.hard_boundary: Prime factorization is an exact reference implementation, not a factoring-speedup theorem. Log embedding is derived and need not be a discrete Euclidean lattice. Full rational gauge information may exceed recurrent loop observables.

methods.name: BRC error linearization / Pell-Pade tail transport
capabilities: exact recursive BRC gap orbit with second difference -2 and third difference 0
exact integer Pell-Pade lower approximant to sqrt((m+h)/m) for h=1,2
second-order linear recurrence in Pade order X_(n+2)=(4m+2h)X_(n+1)-h^2 X_n
exact integer <=2-correction certificate J h^(2n+1)<=m A_n B_n
methods.core_law: For E_K=sqrt(1+x)-1-P_K, derivatives above order K satisfy (1+x)E_K^(n+1)/E_K^n=1/2-n, while ordinary BRC correction gaps satisfy G_q=G_0-q(2a+q). The diagonal Pade/Pell approximant obtained from (1+sqrt(1+x))^(2n+1)=P_n+sqrt(1+x)Q_n yields homogenized integers A_n,B_n with (m+h)B_n^2-mA_n^2=h^(2n+1). This makes A_n/B_n a rigorous lower sqrt-ratio predictor and gives the exact sufficient certificate J h^(2n+1)<=m A_n B_n for at most two BRC basin corrections.
methods.hard_boundary: Classical Pade/Pell approximation is prior art. The current contribution is exact BRC composition, certification, and error-linearization bookkeeping. The Python reference path is substantially faster than the previous high-order Taylor table-free tail but still slower than direct optimized isqrt on isolated steps. No asymptotic factorization speedup, RSA-practicality, optimal multiplier order, or Foundation promotion is claimed.
